title: HMM + RL Regime-Based Allocation on SPY/TLT/GLD Production Portfolio Sleeve
description: Implement the Verma et al. (2026) HMM+RL framework (arXiv:2605.27848) on our production ETF universe, testing it as a regime-switching allocation layer for a SPY/TLT/GLD sleeve of the production portfolio. The paper uses daily ETF data 2004-2025 with a 3-state Gaussian HMM (BIC-selected): Low-Volatility, Transitional, High-Volatility regimes. An RL policy (state = current regime probabilities, action = discrete allocation weights) is trained to maximize Sharpe conditional on regime. Key results: HMM-only outperforms passive SPY; RL+HMM achieves highest Sharpe AND lowest drawdown while remaining interpretable through discrete regime-dependent actions. H383 tests: (1) Replicate 3-state HMM on SPY/TLT/GLD daily data 2004-2026; (2) Train RL policy (PPO or Q-learning) on IS 2004-2017; (3) Evaluate OOS 2018-2026 against H311 EW-4 static blend baseline (OOS Sharpe 1.532, MaxDD -6.0%); (4) Compare to H249 (regime-conditional weights, OOS Sharpe +0.282 improvement). Gate: OOS Sharpe > 1.532 (H311 best variant). IS: 2004-2017, OOS: 2018-2026. Script: backtesting/daily/run_h383_hmm_rl_allocation.py (to be written). Requires: hmmlearn, stable-baselines3.
rationale: This is a direct extension of H249 (regime-conditional portfolio weights, confirmed OOS +0.282) and H311 (static EW-4 diversification, confirmed OOS 1.532). The Verma et al. paper validates HMM+RL on SPY/TLT/GLD — exactly our defensive capital-preservation use case. The RL layer adds adaptability that H249's fixed regime weights lack: instead of hand-tuning SPY/TLT/GLD weights per regime (H249 found IBS weight 33-40% in bear+volatile), RL learns the optimal allocation policy from the regime state. The 3-state HMM (low-vol/transitional/high-vol) maps cleanly onto our VIX<20, 20-25, >25 threshold framework. H251 (3-state HMM confirmed OOS 0.941) showed HMM alone defaults to static; adding RL avoids this. Key risk: RL requires careful OOS discipline — any reward signal using future returns = look-ahead. Must use only filtered (not smoothed) HMM probabilities per Regime Detection Design Note in CLAUDE.local.md.
